title: Form Array by Concatenating Subarrays of Another Array
summary: Given a 2D integer array groups of length n and an integer array nums, determine if you can select n non-overlapping subarrays from nums such that each subarray matches the corresponding element in groups and maintains the order of groups.
statement: Given a 2D integer array groups of length n and an integer array nums, determine if you can select n non-overlapping subarrays from nums such that each subarray matches the corresponding element in groups and maintains the order of groups. Return true if possible, otherwise false.
constraints: Match every group as an exact contiguous subarray of nums in the given order.
Matched groups may not overlap; unused nums elements may appear before, between, or after groups.
reference_solution:
def can_form_from_ordered_groups(groups, nums):
 position=0
 for group in groups:
  while position+len(group)<=len(nums) and nums[position:position+len(group)]!=group:position+=1
  if position+len(group)>len(nums):return False
  position+=len(group)
 return True

hints: For each group, the earliest nonoverlapping match leaves the most suffix space for later groups.
Scan nums from the current position until the group matches, then jump past it.
Return false if a group cannot fit or match; otherwise continue until every group is consumed.
Replacing any later chosen match by the earliest available one cannot hurt subsequent ordered matches, proving the greedy scan.
